# vk v0.2.3

Date: 2026-10-21. Status: Experimental Git release.
Workspace packages `vkrust` and `vkrust-gen` use version 0.2.3; the Rust import
namespace is `vk`. This Git release does not publish to crates.io.

## Summary

All 842 command spellings selected from the pinned paired Khronos registries
now have callable operations, including all 234 core commands through Vulkan
1.4 and 100 aliases of those core commands. This completes pinned callable
coverage; it does not establish Vulkan conformance or production qualification.
The three development commits after v0.2.2 are consolidated into this release.

## Added and improved

- Complete Vulkan 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4 and remaining extension operations, with
  canonical free functions and delegated methods using immutable cached PFNs.
- Preserve native raw pointers, explicit counts, independently nullable arrays,
  initialized output chains, in/out storage and partial outputs for direct
  forwarding. Scalar values retain their native widths. Negative `VkResult`
  values become `CallError::Vulkan`; non-error statuses remain visible.
- Keep reviewed slice/enumeration/handle-returning adaptations. Caller-initialized
  count/fill queries preserve output headers, chains and explicit count protocols.
- Add loaded exact-ABI tests for every new direct forwarder and independent
  tests for optional arrays, sparse output chains, mapped pointer outputs,
  deferred pipeline outputs and insufficient binary output storage.
- Add an independent XML/Rust/C command-prototype oracle; require all
  core-introduced Boolean feature record inventories through Vulkan 1.4.
- Add explicit Vulkan 1.1 feature/query, descriptor-template/base-dispatch and
  Vulkan 1.2 host-query-reset/render-pass2 native profiles.

## Compatibility and migration

This is the explicitly requested patch checkpoint in the Experimental 0.2
line. Correcting malformed generated vendor names changes source spellings;
it is not a claim of universal source compatibility. For example,
`cmd_set_dispatch_parameters_a_r_m` becomes `cmd_set_dispatch_parameters_arm`.
Other corrected acronym groups include AMDX, NVX, GOOGLE, ANDROID, NN and OHOS.
Update operation, method and dispatch-field references to their generated
snake_case names. AMD remains `_amd`. No legacy aliases are retained.
Native C PFN names and ABI layouts are unchanged.

New direct operations deliberately retain native pointer/count/status contracts;
they do not all use the existing reviewed handle-returning or slice convenience
signatures. Inspect the operation's signature and safety contract when adopting
it. A non-error status may still require deferred completion or caller cleanup.
No wrapper initializes, retries, frees or adopts direct-forwarded outputs.

## Verification

The release commit is rebuilt and tested before tagging, using formatting,
strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, workspace/minimal/default tests, rustdoc,
generation freshness/order, registry hashes, rule mirrors and Python oracle
tests. The actual 0.2.3 Cargo archive is built, extracted and exercised through
an external public-consumer test target. The independent pinned-header layout,
command-prototype and feature-capture oracles run against the release tree and
extracted package where applicable.

The same native load/memory workloads run explicitly, followed by separate
core and synchronization validation profiles. Release logs, artifact/source
hashes and exact commands are retained locally in
`target/verification/v0.2.3/`; this directory is ignored and is not distributed
with the Cargo package. The preceding command checkpoint's dated evidence
remains in the repository history.

## Known limitations

Native qualification is limited to the recorded x86-64 Linux Intel HD Graphics
4400/Haswell target, physical API 1.2.354 and Mesa 26.2.3. Mesa reports incomplete
Haswell support. Vulkan 1.3/1.4 GPU execution, presentation, positive video/ray
tracing, external imports/exports, protected-platform C ABI qualification and
other drivers/architectures remain open. Host compilation or mocks do not
qualify those workloads. GPU-assisted validation is not run.

The independent C command-prototype gate covers 775 available core-header
signatures; 67 protected platform or provisional C signatures remain
unqualified by that gate. All 842 independently derived Rust signatures compile.
Feature promotion/equivalence/dependency semantics and lifetime-aware builders
remain open. Operations remain unsafe and require native valid usage.
The integrated allocator remains an experimental separate-allocation baseline,
not VMA parity. No speed or general safety superiority is claimed.

## Upgrade

Use Git tag `v0.2.3` or the local workspace; a Git push does not publish a
crates.io version. Update malformed vendor spellings as described above, retain
explicit destroy/free paths, and run consumer workloads with validation on the
actual target devices. Do not enable unsupported hardware features to exercise
new command coverage.
